Census: 6 rows, 1 account (B3S606537), 2019-01-18 to 2019-01-22, 3 credits and 3 debits, net 0.00, gross 5295.98; Transaction_Description is `ASF` on every row; notes `Fee Reversal` x3 and `Returned Payment` x3, each with a tag naming the account the fee was owed by. Pairing: the 3 credits sit beside a same-day ManAltF reversal of the same Amount and tag (the CRO's table makes ManAltF a flow, so a stated treatment exists for that type); the 3 debits sit beside no row of another type, only the ASF credit of the same tag 4 days earlier. The CRO's research names ASF on 0 lines. (2) Order of work: the decision rule is code (`decide`), committed in 422ae4888c with the census script, the tests and method_r26 BEFORE the re-grade run; no grade, price or return was read to decide it. Before the rule was written, the 6 ASF rows and the account's neighbouring rows were read once (the pairing evidence above); the rule (every row must pair with ONE type of a stated treatment) was written after that read and before any grade. (3) What the pairing fixes and does not: it shows the ASF credit repeats a credit that ManAltF already books and the Returned Payment takes it back, so the six rows net to zero; it does not say whether the vendor counts the credit as client money, a fee or an error correction, and a treatment for the 3 debit rows rests on no source. (4) The re-grade is trivially equal (82593 of 82593 months identical to method_r25).
